blocks.h2: What You Get When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: Fast help and a price first.

blocks.body: Not every plumbing problem has to be fixed at 2 a.m. A dripping faucet, a running toilet or a slow sink can usually wait for a regular appointment. If you can stop the water at a fixture shutoff and the house is otherwise usable, you have time. Call right away when water is spreading, sewage is coming up, the sump pump has failed during rain or there's no way to shut the water off. If you're unsure, call and we'll help you decide.

blocks.h2: Emergency Plumbing Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.answer: Yes. Our phone line is open around the clock.

items.q: My sump pump stopped during a storm. What do I do?
items.answer: Check whether it has power and the float isn't stuck. If it still won't run, call us right away.

items.q: Who do I call if I smell gas?
items.answer: Leave the house and call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside. We'll handle the repair once it's safe.

items.q: Will I know the price first?
items.answer: Yes. You'll approve a flat-rate price before work begins.

items.q: How fast can you get here?
items.answer: Our office is on Greenbrook Boulevard, and we work to get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: Do you charge more at night?
items.answer: You'll know the price and approve it before we start, any time of day.
